title: Tools and ESD safety
summary: The basic repair toolkit, and how to stop static electricity from damaging parts.

sections.heading: The starter toolkit
sections.body: Most beginner repairs need a precision screwdriver set, plastic opening picks, a plastic spudger, a suction cup, tweezers, and a tray to keep screws in order. A heat pad or a heat gun on low softens glue. Isopropyl alcohol of 90% or stronger cleans away old adhesive.

sections.heading: Why plastic tools matter
sections.body: Metal conducts electricity and scratches easily. A metal tool can short a connector, puncture a battery or tear a flex cable. Plastic tools are much safer around batteries and connectors. Save metal tools for jobs like turning screws.

sections.heading: What ESD is
sections.body: ESD stands for electrostatic discharge. It is the same small shock you sometimes feel from a door handle. You often cannot feel a discharge that is still strong enough to damage a chip, and the damage may only show up later.

sections.heading: How to protect the phone
sections.body: Work on an anti-static mat and wear a grounded wrist strap when you can. If you do not have one, touch a grounded metal object before touching the board. Avoid carpets and synthetic clothes. Hold boards by their edges, and keep parts on the mat rather than on plastic bags.

sections.heading: Protect yourself too
sections.body: Wear safety glasses, especially around glass and springs. Use gloves for broken glass. Work in a well-lit, ventilated place, on a clear table with nothing flammable nearby. Keep food and drinks away from your work.

quiz.question: Why are plastic tools used near batteries and connectors?
options: They are less likely to cause shorts or punctures
quiz.explanation: Plastic does not conduct electricity and is less likely to puncture a battery.

quiz.question: What does ESD stand for?
quiz.explanation: ESD means electrostatic discharge, a sudden release of static electricity.

quiz.question: Can static damage a chip even if you feel nothing?
options: Only when the phone is on
quiz.explanation: A discharge too small to feel can still damage a chip, and the fault may appear later.

quiz.question: Where is the best place to keep loose parts during a repair?
quiz.explanation: An anti-static mat protects parts. Plastic bags and carpets can build up static.
